Understanding asynchronous programming

Asynchronous programming allows a program to start a long-running task and still be responsive to other events while that task runs, rather than having to wait until the task has finished.

Why it matters for modern applications

Many functions provided by browsers can take a long time to complete, and therefore are asynchronous. For example, fetching a resource over the network or asking the user to choose a file can block the main thread if they are handled synchronously.

  • Fetch data from a remote server without freezing the page.
  • Read large files in the background.
  • Handle user input while work continues.
const data = await fetch(url);
